title: Comparison of Cartesian edges with fixed target
statement: Use small quasicategories, coherent triangles and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and Cartesian fibrations and edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $u:E\to\Delta^1$ be a Cartesian fibration, with endpoint fibres $P=E_0$ and $D=E_1$. For each $d\in D$ choose a $u$-Cartesian edge $c_d:g(d)\to d$ over $0\to1$. If $e:x\to d$ is another $u$-Cartesian edge over $0\to1$, the space of edges $h:x\to g(d)$ in $P$ together with a coherent triangle $c_dh\simeq e$ over the triangle $(0,0,1)$ is contractible, and every such $h$ is an equivalence in $P$. Every $u$-Cartesian edge over a degenerate edge of $\Delta^1$ is an equivalence in its endpoint fibre.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Theorem 2.3.3.23(1), printed pp. 266-268; Converse condition (ii): passage from the canonical Cartesian edge to all Cartesian edges. Agent expansion of the proof; read online 2026-10-17, WANTED archive in report.md. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.
